findings.title: _copy_clickhouse_legacy had no idempotency guard against ClickHouse's lack of UPSERT
findings.evidence_before: service/app/db/migrations.py::_copy_clickhouse_legacy issued INSERT INTO seg_ch_{dimension}_runs ... SELECT FROM seg_ch_{dimension} with no ON CONFLICT-equivalent guard. Re-running `scripts/migrate_faz11_schema.py --apply` a second time for the same deterministic legacy run_id (app.db.ingest_runs.legacy_run_id is a stable uuid5 of dataset_id+source_hash) would insert duplicate rows into the run-scoped ClickHouse table, since ClickHouse MergeTree INSERT has no upsert/ON CONFLICT semantics (this is documented in docs/RUN_VERSIONING.md itself as the reason chunk resume is chunk-scoped rather than row-scoped elsewhere in the codebase, but the migration copy step didn't follow the same pattern).
findings.fix_summary: _copy_clickhouse_legacy now calls the existing app.db.clickhouse.delete_run(dataset_id, run_id, dimension) helper (already used elsewhere for inactive-run cleanup, with its own _ensure_inactive guard) before each dimension's INSERT SELECT, so every --apply attempt for a given legacy run starts from a clean slate for that run_id.

findings.title: Retry after a failed migration attempt could never succeed, even once the underlying mismatch was fixed
findings.evidence_before: PostgresRunStore.create() uses INSERT ... ON CONFLICT(run_id) DO NOTHING, so on retry (same deterministic legacy_run_id) it never resets a previously 'failed' row back to 'validating'. PostgresRunStore.activate() only succeeds via UPDATE ingest_runs SET status='completed' ... WHERE run_id=%s AND status='validating' and raises RuntimeError('run activation transition failed') when rowcount != 1. Without an explicit reset, every retry after a first failed attempt would hit this RuntimeError unconditionally, regardless of whether the underlying count mismatch was corrected.
findings.fix_summary: apply_migration() now calls store.set_run_status(run_id, 'validating') unconditionally right after store.create(), on every attempt - a harmless no-op on a fresh row, but a real reset on a retried one.
